title: Natural Hazards
seo_title: Grade 4 Natural Hazards Worksheets: Earthquakes, Floods, Tsunamis and Solutions
standard_text: Generate and compare multiple solutions to reduce the impacts of natural Earth processes on humans.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on natural hazards (NGSS 4-ESS3-2): earthquakes, floods, tsunamis, volcanoes and landslides, solutions that reduce damage, and comparing designs using criteria and constraints. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: We cannot stop natural hazards, but we can reduce the damage.
key_sub: Levees, strong buildings, warning systems and evacuation routes protect people. Compare solutions with criteria and constraints.
body_html:
How to think about it

Natural hazards are Earth processes that can harm people: earthquakes, floods, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions and landslides. People cannot stop these processes, but they can reduce their impacts.

  • Earthquakes: flexible buildings, bolting houses down, drills.
  • Floods: levees, houses on stilts, wetlands, not building on low land.
  • Tsunamis: warning buoys and sirens, evacuation routes to high ground.
  • Volcanoes: monitoring and evacuation plans. Landslides: plants and retaining walls.

Engineers compare solutions using criteria (what it must do) and constraints (limits such as cost).

Example

A town by a river floods every spring. Name two solutions.

Keep water out.

Lift homes above the water.

Answer: a levee and houses on stilts

Example

A seawall costs $50 million but the town can spend $20 million. Can they build it?

Cost is a constraint.

50 > 20.

Answer: No, it does not meet the constraint.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking people can stop earthquakes or volcanoes.
  • Choosing the cheapest solution without checking how well it works.
  • Picking a solution made for a different hazard.

faq.a: No. People cannot stop earthquakes, floods or eruptions, but they can design solutions that reduce the damage.

faq.q: How do people reduce flood damage?
faq.a: They build levees and floodwalls, raise houses on stilts, protect wetlands, and avoid building on low land near rivers.
Check which ones meet the criteria (what the solution must do) and the constraints (limits like cost), then choose the best fit.
